restrictions: Two distinct 135-byte messages M(t) = U || 0^40 || U || 0^15, U the 40 little-endian bytes of a 320-bit parameter t, so that with SHA3 padding (byte 135 = 0x86) each message is one absorbed block. t ranges over the cosets t_j + span(W40), j < 256 G, of the 40-dimensional field W40 listed in proof.md Section 3, with the deterministic representatives t_j of Section 6.1 and the Gray order of each coset.

Complete SHA3-256 sponge of sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1: zero initial state, rate 136 bytes, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, rounds 0 to 5 of Keccak-f[1600] in the single permutation call, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with reference operation cost 1626: a six-round call is one unit, every other operation 1/1626; generated straight-line code with immediate addresses, its generation charged in preprocessing (proof.md Section 5.1). N = G Fv + G 4656 2^40 + S_v + 15 Q + 4096 R140 + (2^70 + 16) = 17161635548395357935654921407869734482854 word operations (Section 10); time_log2 = 122.98920 is log2(N/1626) rounded up, by the integer certificate 1626^100000 2^12298919 <= N^100000 < 1626^100000 2^12298920.

Memory below 2^141 words, 2^146 bytes: a direct sparse array of 2^140 words that is never initialized (the sparse-set table is correct for any initial memory, Lemma 8), a dense array of Q words, coset records, work frames and generated code (Section 11.1). Preprocessing at most 2^70 + 16 word operations (below 2^59.34 target compressions), included in time_log2: code generation, constants, the certificate and the deterministic search that produced W40 (Section 11.2). No advice.

Success at least 0.39 rests on one declared heuristic, H_coset: the digests of the enumerated messages, in the algorithm's order, are independent and uniform (proof.md Section 12). Proved in proof.md: two-round affinity on every coset of W40 (780-polarization certificate, recomputed by the experiment), degree at most 8 before the last chi, exactness of the Gray-order finite differences and of their initialization, the sparse-set table for arbitrary initial memory, detection up to a bounded triple event, and every operation count.

No full-scale run and no collision are claimed. The declared experiment executes the schedule at a reduced size (256 cosets per group, the first 2^9 Gray points of each, the full 140-bit key and table) through a counting machine and stops unless every executed count equals the formula of proof.md; its outputs are not evidence of cost or of the premise.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. The full 256-bit digests of the Q = 2^48 G native messages enumerated by CAMP (proof.md Sections 6.1 and 8: G = 1202983983186596773302061 groups h, cosets j = 256 h + c with the deterministic representatives t_j, and in each coset the 2^40 Gray points of span(W40)), taken in CAMP's order, are independent and uniformly distributed. It is used only through three events (Section 9): (i) no two messages share a digest, probability at most 1/T8 with lambda = Q(Q - 1)/2^257; (ii) the number of equal 140-bit-key pairs reaches the verification cap R140, at most 1/4096 by Chebyshev with pairwise independent pair indicators; (iii) a bad triple, expected number at most lambda (Q - 2)/2^140 < 1/4096. With Lemmas 7 to 9 the success probability is greater than 1 - (1/T8 + 2/4096) = 0.3900000000000000000000001211 (exact rational comparison).
heuristics.scope: One ordered sequence of the actual campaign at full size: the deterministic coset representatives t_j, complete 40-dimensional cosets in Gray order, the full 256-bit digest and its 140-bit key projection. Nothing else in the claim is heuristic: two-round affinity, the degree bound, the exactness of the enumeration, the sparse-set table and every operation count are proved in proof.md Sections 3 to 7 and 10.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured on the target function in three preregistered batches (protocols hashed before the runs; pass rule: every count at least expected - 4 sigma; no reruns): 17 runs of 2^30 real six-round SHA3-256 digests, exact equal-pair counts of 32-bit within-coset and 44-bit global projections of each of the four digest lanes. Batches 1 and 2 used complete cosets of 2^20, 2^24 and 2^28 messages of random subspaces of span(W40) with random origins, and random-direction controls; batch 3 used exactly the deterministic sequence of Section 6.1 (cosets j = 0..1023 with the first 20 ordered W40 vectors, j = 0..63 with the first 24). All counts lie within 2.1 sigma of expectation and none below expected - 1.4 sigma; field, control and deterministic runs agree. The extrapolation is from single-lane 32- and 44-bit projections to the 256-bit digest, from 2^30 to Q messages, and from 20- to 28-dimensional subspaces to complete 40-dimensional cosets and all 256 G cosets of the sequence.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption: no proof is known, and image size or balance do not imply it (a balanced linear map can be injective on every translate of a campaign space). On each coset every digest bit has degree at most 16 in the 40 inner variables, a real structure; the tests found no pair deficit at the tested widths but reach neither 256 bits nor complete cosets. The organizer-run experiment checks nothing about H_coset: it executes the schedule at a reduced size and the organizer recomputes the digests of returned pairs (none expected).
